chapters.title: AI Chat
chapters.subtitle: Talk to your assistants in the admin and on your website

steps.text: People talk to an AI assistant in three places: a chat page in the admin, a floating chat on every admin page, and a chat box on your website. This video shows why they exist, how each one works, and how to set them up, including the engines that can power the chat.

chapters.title: Why AI chat
chapters.subtitle: A place to talk to every assistant

steps.text: Once an assistant exists, people need a place to talk to it. Staff want an answer without leaving their work, and visitors want an answer without writing an email.
A chat has to remember the conversation, so a follow-up question makes sense, and it has to keep a history, so nobody asks the same thing twice.
It also has to work where people already are: in the admin, in a corner of every page, and on the public site, limited to the people who are allowed to use it.
The AI Chat module gives you all of that on top of your AI profiles, so an assistant behaves the same way everywhere.

chapters.title: How it is organized
chapters.subtitle: Chat page, admin widget, website widget and engines

steps.text: The chat page is one page for every chat profile, with a history of your own conversations. People open it from the admin menu.
The admin chat widget floats on every admin page, so staff can ask a question without leaving what they are doing. You choose its profile once, in the site settings.
The website chat widget is a normal widget that you place on a layer. It puts an assistant in the corner of your public pages, for visitors.
The engine behind a chat is called an orchestrator. The default one plans each answer, and two optional ones, Claude and GitHub Copilot, can take over for a profile.

chapters.title: Chat with an assistant
chapters.subtitle: Open a chat and ask questions

steps.text: Open Artificial Intelligence, Profiles. Open the Actions menu of a chat profile and click New chat. A profile that has Show on admin menu turned on also appears under Artificial Intelligence in the menu.
A new chat opens with the profile's welcome message. New Chat starts over, and Chat History lists your past chats.
Type a question and press Enter, or click the send arrow. The answer appears as it is written, and it comes from the instructions and the knowledge of the profile.
Ask a follow-up question. The assistant remembers what was said earlier in the same chat, so you do not repeat yourself.
A chat is saved as soon as it starts, with a title that the AI writes from the conversation. Click Chat History to find it later.
Chat History lists your chats with this assistant, newest first. Each row shows its title, its status, and when it was last used.
Type part of a title in History search and click Search to find a chat. Click View, or the title, to open it and continue where you left off.
Actions on a row deletes that one chat. Delete Chat History deletes all of your chats with this assistant. Both ask you to confirm, and each needs its own permission.
New Chat starts over with an empty chat. You only ever see your own chats.

chapters.title: The admin chat widget
chapters.subtitle: An assistant on every admin page

steps.text: Turn on the AI Chat Admin Widget feature, then open Settings, Artificial Intelligence. The Admin Widget section decides which assistant floats on every admin page.
Pick the Chat profile. Choose No profile to hide the widget. Max history sessions and Primary color appear once you pick a profile. Click Save.
Now every admin page has a round chat button in the bottom-right corner. Click it to open the assistant.
Ask a question without leaving the page. The widget has the same message box as the chat page, and its header has New chat and Chat history.
Drag the header to move the window, and drag its edge to resize it. The widget remembers its place, its size, and your current chat on the next page.

chapters.title: The website chat widget
chapters.subtitle: An assistant in the corner of your public pages

steps.text: To put an assistant on your public website, use the Artificial Intelligence Chat widget. Open Design, Widgets. A zone is where a widget lives, here Footer, and a layer decides on which pages it shows.
The Always layer has one rule, a Boolean condition set to true, so its widgets show on every page. Click Edit on a layer to see its rules.
Back on the Widgets page, open Add Widget in the Footer zone and choose Artificial Intelligence Chat.
Give the widget a Title, pick the layer, and pick the Profile it talks to. Total history chat to show sets how many past chats a signed-in visitor can reopen. Click Publish.
Open your website. A round chat button sits in the corner. Visitors who are not signed in use the Anonymous role, so give that role permission to query this one profile, and no other.
Visitors chat the same way. A chat is saved only once the visitor sends a first message, never just because someone opened a page.
The engine that plans an answer and decides which tools to use is called an orchestrator. Settings, Artificial Intelligence has a Default Orchestrator section for the one that comes with the site.
The AI Claude Orchestrator feature adds a Claude section. Choose the Authentication type, API key, enter the key, and pick a Default model. Claude stays off while the type is Not configured.
The AI Copilot Orchestrator feature adds a Copilot section. It signs in as a GitHub signed-in user, or it uses your own API key, with a Provider type, a Base URL and a Default model.
Once an engine is set up, a profile can choose it in the Orchestrator field of its General card. Those engines choose their own model, so the deployment fields of the profile are hidden.
A public assistant is open to anyone, so the site protects it. In the Prompt Security section, checks block messages that try to make the assistant ignore its instructions.

Below them are the limits: how many messages one person can send in a window, and tiers for visitors who are not signed in, such as a short burst and a daily total. Session limits cap how many new chats a visitor can start.
The Visitor Identity section decides how a visitor is recognized across visits, with a cookie. Set the Visitor cookie name and the Cookie lifetime.
A profile can override these limits on its own Prompt Security card. Leave a field empty to keep the site's value.
Staff get an internal helper. A policy assistant is one click away in the admin menu, and every conversation is kept for the person who held it.
Visitors get a website assistant. It answers questions about opening hours, orders and repairs at any time, and hands over when it does not know.
Editors get an admin assistant that is always there. Give its profile tools, and it can look things up on the site while they work.
A team that already uses Claude or GitHub Copilot can pick that engine for one profile, and keep the default for the rest.
A chat page for staff, a floating chat in the admin, and a chat box for visitors, all on the same profiles. Thanks for watching.
